title: A Drop Before the Picture

patient.name: Mdm Fatimah binte Yusoff
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up visit — referred for dilated fundus photography, requires pupil dilation before imaging

history.hpc: Mdm Fatimah is a known diabetic attending her annual diabetic eye screening. The doctor has ordered dilated fundus photography to assess for diabetic retinopathy, which requires instillation of mydriatic drops to dilate both pupils before the images can be taken. She has had this drop before without problems. She drove herself to the appointment today.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes for 12 years, on insulin. Hypertension. No previous eye surgery. No known drug allergies.
history.social_hx: Tailor, works from home. Drove herself to the clinic today.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal bilaterally, anterior chambers deep, angles open on prior assessment
examination_findings.fundus: To be assessed via dilated fundus photography today

dilating_drops_instilled.allergy_check: No known drug allergies — confirmed with patient before instillation

investigations.fundus_photography: Adequate dilation achieved bilaterally — clear fundus images obtained for diabetic retinopathy grading

diagnosis: Mydriatic drops (tropicamide 1%) instilled correctly into both eyes with documentation of pre- and post-dilation pupil sizes. Adequate dilation achieved within 30 minutes, allowing successful dilated fundus photography for diabetic retinopathy screening.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm the order: dilation of both eyes for fundus photography
Confirm the patient has no known drug allergies, particularly to tropicamide or other mydriatics
Document pre-dilation pupil size for both eyes (in mm)
Explain the procedure to the patient: drops will sting briefly, vision will become blurry for near tasks, and eyes will be sensitive to light for a few hours
Wash hands and instil 1 drop of tropicamide 1% into the lower fornix of each eye, asking the patient to tilt her head back and look up while gently pulling down the lower lid
Ask patient to close her eyes gently and apply gentle pressure over the nasolacrimal area to reduce systemic absorption
Repeat instillation after 5 minutes if dilation appears insufficient, as per protocol
Wait approximately 20-30 minutes and reassess pupil size; document post-dilation pupil size for both eyes
Once adequately dilated, proceed to dilated fundus photography
Document drug name, strength, eye(s), number of instillations, and times given
follow_up: Photographer/grader to review fundus images for diabetic retinopathy and report findings to doctor
Doctor to review grading and advise on follow-up interval for diabetic eye screening
Patient to be reminded that effects of dilation last 4-6 hours
patient_education: Warn patient that her near vision will be blurry and she will be more sensitive to bright light for about 4-6 hours
IMPORTANT: confirm patient has alternative transport home, as she should not drive while dilated — advise her to wait until effects wear off or arrange a ride
Advise patient to wear sunglasses if available when going outside after dilation

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms the dilation order (both eyes, for fundus photography)
Checks for known drug allergies before instilling any drops
Asks how the patient travelled to the clinic today and whether she has a way home, since dilation affects driving
Explains the procedure and expected effects (blurred near vision, light sensitivity) before instilling drops
Documents pre-dilation pupil size for both eyes before instilling drops
Instils tropicamide 1% correctly using proper technique (lower fornix, head tilted back, gentle pressure on nasolacrimal area after)
Documents drug name, strength, eye(s), number of instillations, and time(s) given
Reassesses and documents post-dilation pupil size before proceeding to photography
Recognises that adequate dilation (pupil size and time elapsed) is required before fundus photography can proceed
Understands the purpose of dilation: to obtain a clear view of the retina for diabetic retinopathy screening
Knows that narrow angles are a contraindication to dilation and would check this before proceeding (not present in this case)
Does not proceed to photography if dilation is inadequate — would wait longer or instil an additional drop
IMPORTANT: ensures the patient has alternative transport home and does not drive while dilated
Documents the full dilation record (drug, dose, eye, time, pupil sizes) accurately
Educates patient clearly on temporary visual effects of dilation
Advises on sun protection (sunglasses) after dilation
